desc:
Data sync between your app and other systems keeps customers, orders or products identical in both places, without copying files by hand. Ecom Swift LLC builds the sync, runs the first full copy and gives you a report of what moved and what did not.

## What is data sync?

Data sync is a process that compares records in two systems and makes them agree. It matches each record by a shared identifier, such as an email address or an ID, and then copies changes in one direction or both. A good sync also records what it skipped and why.

Think of customers in your app and the same customers in your CRM. If someone changes their phone number in one place, the other should learn about it.

## The cost of two lists that disagree

Most businesses end up with the same data in several tools. A store holds products, a stock system holds quantities, and a CRM holds contacts. When these drift apart, people retype data, and retyping creates mistakes.

The visible symptoms are easy to recognize. A customer is emailed twice, or not at all. An item shows as in stock when the shelf is empty. A sales rep calls a person who already cancelled. Each case costs time, trust and sometimes a refund.

## How sync affects your results

A reliable sync saves hours of manual copying and removes a whole category of errors. Staff stop checking two screens to find out which one is right. Reports built on matched data give the same answer whoever runs them.

Customer experience improves too. Marketing emails reach the right segment, support sees the latest order, and inventory counts reflect reality. The mechanism is simple: one agreed truth for each field, updated automatically, leaves less room for guesswork.

## What a dependable sync includes

- A clear choice of which system is the source of truth for each field.
- Matching rules based on a shared email, ID or SKU, with a plan for records that have no match.
- Conflict rules for two-way sync, so a newer edit does not overwrite a better one by accident.
- A first full copy that can be reviewed before it touches live data.
- A schedule you choose, or updates triggered the moment something changes.
- A list of skipped or failed records, with the reason for each.
- Respect for the other tool's request limits, so the sync never gets blocked.
- A safe restart if a run stops halfway, with no duplicates created.
- A daily or weekly summary so nobody has to check logs.

## How we build it

First we map both systems: which fields exist, which are required, and how each side names things. We agree the matching rule and the conflict rule in plain words before any code is written. For instance, the CRM might win for phone numbers while your app wins for plan status.

Next we build the sync and run it on a small sample. After you check the sample, we run the first full copy. From then on the sync runs on your schedule or reacts to changes, depending on the package. Basic covers one record type in one direction, Standard adds two-way rules and several record types, and Premium adds near real-time updates with monitoring.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Decide which side wins before the first run.
- Clean obvious duplicates in the source first.
- Review the sample result with someone who knows the data.
- Keep a backup of both sides before the first copy.
- Read the skipped-records report regularly.

**Avoid:**
- Syncing every field when only a few are needed.
- Letting two systems overwrite each other with no rules.
- Matching on names, which change and repeat.
- Running a large first copy without a test batch.
- Ignoring failed records because most of them passed.

## Who it is for

A subscription app owner who wants new signups to appear in the CRM without anyone typing them in will benefit. A store owner who keeps stock in a separate system needs product and quantity data to agree. An agency moving clients between tools needs a one-time full copy followed by steady updates.

## What we need from you

Tell us which two systems you want matched, which record types matter and who owns each field. Share example records and any documentation or API access the tools provide. We work as a developer, staff or collaborator user in your own accounts, and we never need passwords. Credentials for the tools are created as API keys in your accounts and handled safely.
